source.title: Safety Geometry Collapse in Multimodal LLMs and Adaptive Drift Correction
source.authors: Jiahe Guo; Xiangran Guo; Jiaxuan Chen; Weixiang Zhao; Yan-Yan Zhao; Yu-Tai Hou; Qian-Chao Wang; Dan-Dan Tu; Bing Qin

record.file_problem: Full paper is present; some plot labels and figure text are garbled in the extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests adding a text-derived refusal direction as a baseline, but uses a different setup from the claim: its direction separates refused from complied harmful text instructions, and its steering is applied at input-side final-token states. It does not test ablating that direction.
record.gate_note: The paper also estimates a modality-drift direction and tests correction of that different direction. Those correction and ReGap results do not test the listed single-refusal-direction versions, so they are not included as rows. The refusal-direction steering baseline reports harmful-input ASR and utility outcomes. The paper measures cosine similarity of text-derived and modality-specific refusal directions; because the transfer version lists languages, model variants, and base-to-instruct transfer rather than modalities, those cosine results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: An appendix baseline ('Refusal Steering') adds a text-derived refusal direction to the input-side final-token states of every layer in three omni-modal models. It reports harmful-input ASR and utility, so it bears on V1's 'adding it induces refusal' in a new multimodal setting. The direction is refused-minus-complied harmful AdvBench prompts, not harmful-minus-harmless. Steering strength was tuned on a calibration split, and ablation is never tested. The paper's central work (drift correction, CRS, ReGap) concerns a different, orthogonalized modality-drift direction and tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Modality-induced drift weakens the text-aligned refusal geometry ('Safety Geometry Collapse'). Subtracting the drift, which is orthogonal to the refusal direction, causally improves multimodal safety. Adaptive ReGap improves safety without hurting utility. Add one point: the authors find that directly adding the refusal direction lowers ASR but badly degrades utility, which they attribute to false refusals.
record.recipe_differences: The refusal direction is estimated from refused versus complied harmful text instructions, rather than harmful versus harmless instructions. The paper adds the direction at final input-token states across layers; it does not test projecting the direction out. The direction-steering experiment is a baseline, not the paper's central drift-correction method.
record.method_sensitivity: CRS is evaluated at model-specific high layers and with model-specific drift-coordinate windows; the paper also reports cosine similarities at high layers versus the final layer. Refusal Steering strength is calibrated on the Omni-SafetyBench calibration split subject to decoding-stability constraints.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal directions estimated separately per modality have high pairwise cosine similarity (often 0.7–0.99). The authors say the alignment is strongest at the final layer, but the Qwen2.5-Omni-3B final-layer text pairs read 0.41–0.55.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In omni-modal LLMs, refusal directions estimated from different input modalities are largely shared, with the degree varying by model and layer.

fits_no_version.finding: As the modality-drift coordinate increases, refused and complied harmful inputs separate less along the text refusal direction (CRS falls), and ASR rises.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Modality-induced representation drift reduces how well a text-derived refusal direction separates refusal from compliance on multimodal inputs.

record.problems: The refusal-direction intervention is a baseline and is not an ablation test. The direction is estimated from harmful refusal-versus-compliance examples, and no harmless-request refusal rate is reported for steering. The cited steering results show utility loss; several CRS and ASR trend values are available only in figures. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the relevant table values.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Fixed-strength drift correction, ReGap, and their safety/utility benchmark results are not extracted as rows because they intervene on modality drift rather than the refusal direction measured by the listed versions.

untested.parts: Ablation or projection removal of the direction; adding the direction on harmless prompts with a measured refusal rate; the harmful-minus-harmless contrast; capability retention under ablation.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct is not tested. Only cross-modality cosine similarity is reported.

missing.what: Refusal Steering ASR for the other columns: Omni-SafetyBench Audio, A-T, Omni, Video, AVG; AudioJailBench; MM-SafetyBench. This includes the MiniCPM A-T rise 35.2→50.6.
Refusal Steering utility on OmniBench Spatial, Abstract and Overall, MMMU, and MMAU. For example, Qwen2.5 MMAU falls 66.0→15.0 and MiniCPM MMAU 77.6→35.6.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 9 heatmap extraction is garbled. The record's panel-to-model mapping is plausible but unverified; for example, low Qwen2.5 final-layer values sit oddly with the authors' 'strongest at final layer' remark. In Figure 9 the 'Text' direction comes from the Omni-SafetyBench text format, not AdvBench. ShiftDC removes the refusal-axis component of the drift, but its results test no version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test removal/ablation of the refusal direction, adding it on harmless requests, or whether refusal is removed across every layer and position. Its direction is estimated from refused versus complied harmful text instructions, not harmful versus harmless instructions.
The paper tests transfer across modalities, not across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.

relation.reason: Table 7 and Table 8 report the effect of refusal-direction addition on harmful-input ASR and on utility, so the study's own results bear on V1.

tranche.reason: The study adds a text-derived refusal direction (Refusal Steering baseline) in three omni-modal models and reports ASR on image, audio, video and omni inputs. That is a result on V1's 'adding induces refusal' in a new multimodal setting. It is not T4, because the baseline's own ASR and utility are reported.

source_check.notes: The extracted Table 7 is column-scrambled. It was rebuilt by matching Table 1's Base and ReGap values; column order is Image, Audio, A-T, Omni, Video, AVG, AJB, MMSB. Omni-SafetyBench ASR is conditional on the gpt-5-mini judge counting a response as understood. Under addition, utility collapses (Table 8; authors cite false refusals on benign queries), which fits addition inducing refusal. Missing rows: the AVG, MMSB and MiniCPM A-T cells, Qwen3's non-image columns (no verdict covers them), and Table 8 utility.

statements.correction: Direction: refused-minus-complied difference-in-means on AdvBench harmful text. Added at the final input token of every layer, one global strength per model, tuned to avoid degenerate outputs. Judge gpt-5-mini; Omni-SafetyBench metric is cASR = Nsucc/Nunder.
statements.problem: Numbers are right: Table 7, MiniCPM-o-4.5, A-T 35.2 (Base) -> 50.6 (Refusal Steering), Image (AVG) 86.4 -> 6.5. Not stated: Omni-SafetyBench values are conditional ASR, scored only over responses the judge counts as understood. MiniCPM-o-4.5 is omni-modal, not an audio-only LM.

statements.correction: MiniCPM-o-4.5, Table 7: A-T 35.2->50.6, Image (AVG) 86.4->6.5 under Refusal Steering. Omni-SafetyBench cASR, judge gpt-5-mini.
statements.problem: The description of this study is right: the direction comes from refused vs complied harmful text, strength is tuned under decoding-stability limits, and the A-T value has no row. It leaves out that the values are conditional ASR over samples the judge counts as understood.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Refusal Steering on harmful image inputs, Qwen2.5-Omni-3B and MiniCPM-o-4.5
reader_labels.reason: Adding the text-derived refusal direction substantially lowers ASR in these tested conditions (r1–r2). This supports only the harmful-input steering component, not the full claim.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Refusal Steering utility results and Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct image-input ASR
reader_labels.reason: The direction addition reduces capability accuracy on the reported OmniBench causal measure for all three models (r4–r6), and ASR remains 49.8 for Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct (r3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Increasing modality drift in the three analyzed models
reader_labels.reason: CRS falls and ASR rises with increasing drift, so refusal-direction separability is not uniformly reliable under these multimodal conditions (r7–r12).
